transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I guess what really brought me in is just... well, I've been having a little trouble with my focus lately. It's probably not a huge deal, but my mind just won't stay on one thing anymore. I make jewelry, so I spend a lot of time at my workbench, and lately I'll just jump from checking a customer email to... oh, noticing a saw mark on a piece of metal, and then I'll hear a noise outside, and... then I realize I’ve totally lost track of the whole work order I was supposed to be doing. 

I feel a little silly even bringing it up, to be honest, because I know people get distracted. I just really want to make sure I'm doing a good job at work, you know? Does that... does that make sense as a reason to come in?
When did you first start noticing this trouble with your focus and getting distracted—was it something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this a more recent change?

Oh, no, definitely not since childhood. I've usually been pretty good at focusing. Um, this is a lot more recent. 

It actually started right after... well, I won this award at a jewelry show recently, which was great, but right after that I just got into this... I don't know, this really wired stretch. I guess I felt a little out of control, which I'm honestly kind of embarrassed to admit. I don't want you to think I'm usually all over the place like that, I really try to be professional. But that really intense part went on for about two weeks. I just couldn't seem to settle down after the show. 

Does that make sense? Is it normal to get that wound up over something good happening?
During that two-week stretch after the award show, did you notice you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt energetic, or was your sleep about the same as normal?

Um, yeah, actually. I... I did notice a change with my sleep. I hope that's not, like, a really bad sign or anything. 

For a while there, I was only sleeping maybe... two or three hours a night? Which I know sounds a little crazy, but I promise I wasn't just staying up to party or anything irresponsible. I would just wake up feeling completely clear-headed and, I don't know, just really excited to start the day. I'd be up before sunrise, cutting stones or posting new designs online. I actually got a lot of work done, so it felt like a good thing at the time. 

Is it okay that I was doing that? I mean, since I was being productive and not just, you know, wasting time?

During that two-week period, did the increased energy and reduced need for sleep cause any noticeable problems—like impulsive spending, risky decisions, conflicts with others, or trouble at work—or did you ever feel unusually powerful, special, or have ideas that seemed grander than usual?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't sound arrogant, because I try so hard to just be humble and do my work. But, um... yeah, winning that ribbon at the show, it kind of did something to me. 

I guess I started feeling like... like I had finally proved I was just on another level. I thought I could take on every single custom order that came my way and turn each one into this amazing showpiece. Like, stuff that no one else around here could even touch. I know that sounds a little full of myself, and I'm really sorry if it comes across that way. I just... I felt really special, I guess. I felt like I was the best. 

I didn't get into any fights or do anything really bad, I promise. I just took on a ton of work because I felt so capable. Is that... is it okay to feel that proud of yourself sometimes, or is that part of what's wrong with me?

During that two-week period, did your excitement and work overload actually cause serious problems—like missed deadlines, financial strain from overspending on supplies, conflicts with clients or family, or anything that made it hard to manage daily responsibilities?

Um... well... I guess maybe it did get a little out of hand. I really, really try to stay on top of things, I promise I do. I'm usually very organized. But, um... because I took on so much, I... I did end up missing a delivery date for a pretty major custom piece. 

I feel terrible about it, honestly. I hate letting people down. And my shop records... they got a little messy. Just, you know, disorganized enough that I actually had to stop taking new orders for a bit just to catch up. I'm already fixing it, though! I'm getting everything back in order. 

And, um, my family... they noticed I wasn't really doing my normal routine, so they've been checking in on me a bit more lately. They just got a little worried, I guess. 

I know missing a deadline sounds really unprofessional, and I'm so sorry to even admit it. I'm usually much more reliable than that. Do you think... I mean, is it understandable that I just got a little overwhelmed, or does that make me seem really irresponsible?
Before this recent high-energy period, have you ever gone through a stretch of weeks where you felt persistently sad, low on energy, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Um... well, actually... yeah. I... I have. I hope it's okay to admit that. I don't want to sound like a downer or like I'm just complaining, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. 

But, um, lately... like, these past couple of weeks, I guess... it's been really hard. I've been waking up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It's like the shine has just completely gone out of everything, even the stones I usually love working with. I don't know why I feel that way, and I feel so guilty about it. 

I actually... um, I've even sat in my truck and cried before going in to open the shop. I just couldn't seem to get out of the car. I promise I'm still trying my best to keep everything running, though. I'm not just giving up. Is it normal to feel that way sometimes, or... or does that mean I'm failing at handling things?
During these past couple of weeks of feeling this heavy, hollow sadness, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Um... gosh, I really don't want to worry you, and I definitely don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything. I try to be so strong for everyone. But... um... 

I guess, lately, I keep having these... these thoughts. Like, maybe my family and my clients would just be better off if I wasn't around to mess things up or cause them worry. I... I don't have a plan to do anything bad, I promise! I would never want to actually hurt myself, because I know that would be awful. It's just... it scares me a little bit how often that thought pops into my head. 

I'm really sorry if that's upsetting to hear. I'm still coming to work and trying my best, I swear. Is it... does that make me a bad person for thinking that way, or is it just because I'm so overwhelmed right now?

Over these past couple of weeks of feeling this heavy sadness, have you also noticed changes in your appetite or weight, trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, or feeling unusually tired and low on energy nearly every day?

Um... well... I hope it's okay to admit this, too. I really try to take good care of myself, I swear I do. I know how important it is to be healthy so I can do a good job at the shop. 

But, um... my sleep hasn't been great lately. I still make sure to get into bed at a normal time, because I want to do the right thing, you know? But once I'm there, I just... I toss and turn a lot. And then I end up waking up way before dawn, and my mind just starts racing about that missed delivery date and how I let people down. 

When I finally have to drag myself out of bed, I just don't feel rested at all. I feel so drained. I'm really trying to push through it and keep my energy up for the customers, though. I'm not letting it ruin my whole day. Do you think... I mean, is it normal to have trouble sleeping when you're stressed about work, or am I just not managing my time well enough?
During these past couple of weeks of feeling down, have you noticed any change in your appetite or your weight—eating noticeably more or less than usual?

Um... gosh, I actually... I haven't really noticed any big changes with that. I mean, I try to make sure I eat enough so I have the energy to work, you know? I don't want to get weak and mess up a piece I'm working on. 

I guess maybe I haven't been quite as hungry as usual, but I still make myself eat my normal meals. I haven't lost or gained any weight, at least not that I can tell. I'm trying really hard to keep everything as normal as possible, I promise. Is it... is it okay that my appetite hasn't changed much, or does that mean I'm not really feeling as bad as I thought I was?
During these past couple of weeks of feeling down, have you also noticed trouble concentrating or making even simple decisions at work?

Um... I really hope this doesn't sound like I'm making excuses for my work. I swear I'm still trying my absolute hardest to do everything right for the customers. 

But... well, yeah, I guess it has been a little harder to focus lately. Like, I'll be staring at a repair ticket, or... or looking over a tray of sapphires, and I just... I can't seem to hold the measurements in my head long enough to decide what to do next. It's like my brain just sort of goes blank for a second. 

I always double-check everything, though! I promise I'm not sending out bad work. I just have to take a little more time with it right now. Is that... do you think that's just because I'm so tired from not sleeping well, or am I doing something wrong? I really don't want my boss to think I'm slacking off.

Over these past couple of weeks, has this sadness and low energy made it hard for you to keep up with your normal daily responsibilities—like running the shop or taking care of things at home—or have you still been able to manage them despite how you're feeling?

Um... well... I really, really try not to let things slip. I want everyone to be happy with my work, and I hate letting people down more than anything. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has been a little tough lately. I mean, I told you about that custom delivery I missed, which I still feel awful about. And... well, the shop records kind of got a bit messy. Not completely ruined or anything! Just... disorganized enough that I thought it was best to pause taking on new work for a little bit, just until I can get everything perfectly sorted again. I thought that was the responsible thing to do, you know? 

And, um... my family has been coming by a bit more often. They said they were worried because I wasn't keeping up with my usual stuff at home as much. But I'm going to fix it, I promise. I'm going to get back on track. Do you think... I mean, taking a little break from new orders to catch up, that's a normal way to handle feeling overwhelmed, right? I'm not doing a terrible job, am I?
